title: A comment after a key with no value stays on the key's line when the value becomes a block collection
notes: `a:` has no value, so it reads as null, and `# c` is a comment on its line (section 6.6). Replacing the null with a mapping holding a sequence writes the new collection below the key. The comment is outside the value and edits do not touch comments outside the value (docs/edit-semantics.md, Comments), so it stays after `a:`. The specification allows flow collections as well, and no sibling gives a layout to copy, so the layout rests on the kit's rule for a new nested block collection: the mapping is indented by the document's block indentation step, two spaces when no nested mapping gives another, and the sequence under `k` by the same step again. Tag `convention`.

provenance.reference: A patch engine that moved the comment of a key with no value below the new collection, or dropped it.
